# PRD 004: Hub layouts

<a id="why"></a>

## Why

Nodes still sit on top of one another even at maximum spacing, and the logical fan-out is not readable. The operator wants the shape of an Obsidian graph: hubs with their things fanned around them, while unrelated nodes are free to settle where their links take them.

The view already has force layout, spacing, similarity links and a spine with its own spread control. PR #71 kept a 747-node, 30-band spine from becoming a thin strip; PR #58 reduced per-graph fetch time from 1.9-13 seconds to 0.05-0.4 seconds. Hub layouts must keep those gains, not add a second round of graph reads or flatten a timeline into circles.

A layout hub is not always a declared hub. Degree and similarity suggest centres for a view. PRD 003 rules-15, rules-33 and rules-34 define real hubs through named-node or type-hub declarations and serve their membership relations to the view. Every edge of the declared relation into a hub node counts as membership, whether hand-added or auto-added. This PRD keeps that boundary visible and does not implement backend hub declarations or membership writes.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

| id | goal |
| --- | --- |
| g-1 | Nodes have room at sensible defaults, and spacing visibly increases that room. |
| g-2 | Several hubs and their neighbours read as separate fans, with everything else free to settle by its links. |
| g-3 | Every layout works with a spine or without one, and the same graph and settings give the same result. |

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non goals

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| ng-1 | Backend hub-declaration and auto-add behaviour belong to PRD 003. The view creates no hub node type and performs no graph mutation to produce a layout. |
| ng-2 | New embeddings, an all-pairs similarity calculation, a new daemon endpoint or a wire-format change. Any later need for new served data must be agreed separately. |
| ng-3 | Copying Obsidian's whole interface, replacing the renderer, or adding a graph-editing feature. |
| ng-4 | Showing every label at every zoom. Labels may be withheld when crowded; visible nodes must not be hidden to make the layout pass. |
